title: Browser tool exposure
objective: Expose only live-qualified browser shapes through the explicit browser_structured profile with no implicit widening of existing profiles, no remote mapping, and continued absence of browser_evaluate, arbitrary JavaScript, generic CDP, personal-profile control, raw process control, and generic filesystem authority. Tool discovery, documentation, profile tables, OAuth scope tables, and runtime implementation must agree mechanically.

include: explicit browser_structured profile with only live-qualified shapes
mechanical agreement across tool discovery, documentation, profile tables, OAuth scope tables, and runtime
proof that no existing profile widens implicitly
proof that remote browser mapping remains disabled
parity tests for every exposed and denied shape

authority_delta.process: None beyond the SG-000074 Deskal-supervised low-authority browser child process family.
authority_delta.network: None beyond SG-000075 governed navigation decisions for the isolated host.
authority_delta.browser: Exposure metadata only for already-qualified shapes. No new capability.
authority_delta.approval: None. Exposure changes no approval semantics.

invariants: discovery, docs, profiles, scopes, and runtime agree exactly
no profile widens without its own governed grain

acceptance.claim: Only live-qualified shapes appear under browser_structured with mechanical parity across discovery, docs, profiles, scopes, and runtime, proven by parity tests.
Existing profiles do not widen, remote mapping stays disabled, and browser_evaluate, arbitrary JavaScript, generic CDP, personal-profile, process, and filesystem shapes stay absent.
Exact-head CI, genuine TypeSafe Jev, Alibaba Open Code Review, manual review of excluded files, and zero unresolved review threads all pass.

successor_requirements.sg_000080: SG-000080 may activate only after SG-000079 closes canonically with qualified exposure as its base.

done_when: Qualified browser exposure exists under browser_structured with full parity and no widening, proven by parity tests.
